summary:
Soo, Our project is OptiTone, which is a browser-based EXTENSION and an intelligent scientific music engine. 
Our platform combines a browser extension and a standalone Demo Studio to identify supported scientific sources, extract visual and numerical features, and organise them into a Scientific Feature Representation (SFR). Unlike conventional sonification, It also preserves units, timestamps, spatial context, uncertainty and data provenance, distinguishing actual measurements from metadata, calibrated visual estimates and visual proxies.

Its semantic mapping engine interprets scientific phenomena and selects meaningful auditory representations. Our extended vision introduces a Scientific Musical Composition Engine that can use Indian classical musical grammar, including ragas, talas, melodic structures and instrumentation, to create distinctive compositions based on each dataset's scientific identity. Changes in intensity, periodicity, spatial distribution and significant events influence how the music evolves, while an auditory legend explains what listeners are hearing.

A traditional jukebox plays existing music, whereas OptiTone turns scientific information into music. Every dataset can have a recognisable, evidence-informed musical identity, making Earth science more accessible, engaging and intuitive while connecting scientific discovery with musical expression.
details:
OptiTone is an intelligent scientific sonification platform that converts NASA Earth science visualisations, videos and datasets into meaningful, synchronised audio experiences.

How it works :
OptiTone uses a browser extension and a standalone Demo Studio to analyse supported scientific sources. It extracts information such as intensity, colour, spatial distribution, motion and temporal changes, organising it into a Scientific Feature Representation (SFR) that preserves scientific context, uncertainty and data provenance. Its semantic mapping engine then translates these features into sound, with an auditory legend explaining what listeners hear.

Key innovations :

  • Scientific Feature Representation: Supports different data types, including scalar values, spatial grids, events, vectors and time series.
  • Scientific integrity: Distinguishes actual measurements, published metadata, calibrated visual estimates and visual proxies.
  • Semantic mapping: Selects sounds based on the meaning and relationships of scientific features rather than arbitrary frequency assignments.
  • Indian musical composition: Our extended direction introduces ragas, talas, melodic structures and suitable instruments to generate original compositions influenced by scientific data.
  • Unique musical identities: Different datasets can produce distinct compositions based on their scientific characteristics, with music evolving as the underlying data changes.
  • Synchronised audio: Sound responds to changes and significant events in the visualisation.

Benefits and intended impact :

OptiTone improves accessibility to complex scientific information, supports auditory learning and makes NASA's Earth science discoveries more engaging. It aims to help users understand patterns and changes through sound, including those that may be difficult to identify visually.

Technology used :

TypeScript, JavaScript, React, Vite, Chrome Manifest V3, Web Audio API, Tone.js, Web Workers, Vitest, Git and GitHub.

Development considerations :

We considered scientific accuracy, data provenance, uncertainty, accessibility, audio quality, synchronisation, browser security and cross-origin restrictions. We also prioritised performance on standard hardware, fallback demonstrations when live capture is unavailable, and the use of original, appropriately licensed musical content.
